data.name: Trial by Viking
data.detailed_description:
As an agent of Odin, you will dive into cavernous dungeons hunting for treasure, race for your life from surprise traps, and have vicious axe battles with blood-thirsty kobolds. Loki has left some tricky obstacles in your path, but you will find specialized equipment, trusty friends, and many secrets to help along the way. If you make it far enough, you will even learn to dash through enemies, jump off of walls, and fly swinging through the air using your trusted grappling hook. Are you Viking enough to face the worst terrors the nine worlds have to offer?

Features

  • Acquire special equipment to help you access new and secret areas
  • Character points allow you to specialize your character's stats
  • Morph into a polar bear
  • Keys, switches, gears, air vents, ropes, hidden areas, puzzles, and other tricky elements
  • Control a flying Valkyrie as you swoop through mazes of hazards
  • Power ups like mini Viking, metal Viking, and time slow
  • Ride on the claws of a great owl like a zip line
  • 27 Epic boss battles
  • Sail a Viking long boat while having axe battles with orcs
  • Narrative decisions that will steer your fate toward one of two final boss battles
  • Occasionally-crazy ragdoll physics
  • Controller support
  • 130 different areas to explore
  • Available on Win/Mac/Linux

"With an incredible variety of combat abilities, equippable weapons, abilities, and passives, the game will both empower and challenge the ever-loving crap out of you. This is a compelling universe with fantastic art, music, and tons of content that’s not to be missed" - Seattle Indies Expo jury

"This game has some of the best level design I have ever seen for a platformer" - The Insatiable Gamer

Winner - 2015 Taco Bell Indie Game Garage
Official Selection - Indie MEGABOOTH 2016 PAX East
Nominated for Best Desktop Game - 2016 Game Connection Development Awards

data.short_description: As an agent of Odin, you will dive into cavernous dungeons hunting for treasure, race for your life from surprise traps, and have vicious axe battles with blood-thirsty kobolds. If you like action-packed side-scrolling adventures, you won't want to miss Trial by Viking.

reviews.review:
You are the viking, a hero who probably wouldn't look out of place in [i]Final Fantasy 4[/i]'s Dwarven Kingdom. I mean, just look at that magnificent beard. Anyway, you've been summoned by Odin to rid Asgard of Loki's minions. The story is a standard Norse tale, but the final boss being determined by choices made at pivotal moments in the plot is a nice touch. Oh what am I saying? Not even one paragraph into the review and I'm already talking about the end. So let's step back for just a minute.

Your progress in [i]Trial by Viking[/i] is determined not just by being able to reach the end of the 100+ levels. You also have to find sun-crystals. These shiny gems are used to purchase abilities, tools, and weapon-upgrades. This is one of the interesting aspects of this game. Eventually you'll need certain items in order to progress, but there's nothing stopping you from getting them early, in order to make certain levels easier. However, you also have to be considerate of the fact that there are only so many crystals in each level. You can't expect to repeat levels in order to farm them. 

Before I start discussing the controls, I want to briefly touch on Super Metroid. As fantastic as this game is, its controls could be considered "floaty" by some people. The jump physics, while extremely flexible, might even frustrate a handful of gamers. I think that this is a unique quality, and the identity it helps create is part of the reason why Super Metroid is so revered. [i]Trial of Viking[/i] has controls that are quite different as well, which also gives it an identity of its own. Now if you're thinking that I might be giving this game a little too much credit, by comparing it to a genre-stalwart, then you're probably right. 

The Viking in this game moves in a very loose manner. Moving around will take time to get used to, and for some players, the pure-platforming levels are going to be especially difficult. However, this can work to your advantage. If you get some momentum going, you can quickly move past a lot of danger. Also, unlike some other games, taking damage typically won't knock you into the nearest pit. You'll get pushed around, but you have ample time to recover. You might even purposely get hurt just to give yourself a little boost. Oh and even though there are a wealth of spikes in most levels, they don't cause instant-death.

All that said, if you're playing with an Xbox 360 controller, I highly recommend that you change the dead-zone settings.

For the most part, the level-design in this game is great. Each area is well-paced, and offers a good mixture of puzzles, traps, and monsters to contend with. The tools are all very effective, and it's not too much trouble to switch between mid-level. You can expect to use bombs to destroy walls, daggers to hit far-away switches, and so on. The one trap I don't like is the dark hole. These appear very late in the game, and you're liable to struggle for awhile until you figure it out. It's odd to learn a new mechanic far into the game, especially since it only makes a few appearances. Aside from those annoying holes, I don't have any complaints about the level-design. 

Unfortunately, the melee combat isn't particularly good. There are numerous ranged options, including throwing your axe, that help mitigate the problem. Until you get used to how the game operates, you'll clumsily bump into the monsters. Basically, there's not a lot of finesse to fighting. For most of the bosses, you'll learn patterns and figure out strategies. Still, that doesn't mean you won't run into a few bruisers that fall to relentless attack-button mashing. Anothing thing to keep in mind is that your survival rate is liable to go up, if you ignore certain monsters. A key aspect to keep in mind is that there aren't any ambushes. Monsters won't appear out of thin air nor will they respawn, unless they're summoned by others. It might be worth clearing the area of danger, so you can explore at your leisure. 

Altogether, [i]Trial by Viking[/i] is not only a pretty good game; it also offers a fresh spin on the "Metroidvania" genre. Instead of one large world, there are many small levels, and you have to purchase your upgrades. The controls aren't perfect, but they have their own appeal. Most gamers shouldn't have too much trouble adjusting. 

In short: I'm impressed.
